title: Occupational Work Experience for Mechatronic Technology
description: This course is designed for students working in the Mechatronics industry. The student is required to attend an orientation at the beginning of the course. One semester unit of credit will be awarded for every 54 hours of work experience Students may earn a maximum of 16 units of occupational work experience during their community college attendance. Note: Students must be working in a job or volunteer position related to the Mechatronics industry.
outcomes: Identify, Create, and Implement one SMART learning objective that will include new or expanded occupational/career workplace skills, knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and/or responsibilities.
Apply critical thinking, technology competence and problem solving skills to solve workplace problems.
Develop and apply professionalism and work ethics skills including personal accountability, time management, punctuality, and effective communication.
objectives: Develop Communication skills and professionalism in face-to-face meetings between instructor and employer and with fellow workers.
Apply knowledge gained in the classroom to improve employment skills under actual working conditions.
Develop SMART (Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, Timely) learning objectives.
content: Technology Competence in the Work Place
assignments: Examples: Write a report in which you reflect upon the learning objectives for your Work Experience Position; Complete short written assignments and reports; Present a summary of experiences had on-the-job.
Example: Work with the on-site supervisor and your instructor to develop a specific SMART learning objective. Identify opportunities related to the position.
Example: Evaluate your on-the-job learning and evaluate your performance in relationship to the objectives established for your position.
